aliases.name: OTs-14-4A Groza-4
aliases.note: The 9x39mm model, and the one this entry describes.

aliases.name: OTs-14-1A Groza-1
aliases.note: The 7.62x39mm model, also known as TKB-0239.

massEmpty.sourceNote: OTs-14-4A-01, the rifle configuration with the vertical foregrip fitted in place of the grenade launcher. With the launcher instead, the same source gives 3.97 kg.

length.sourceNote: OTs-14-4A-01. The source gives 610 mm for the grenade-launcher configuration, 500 mm for the -02 carbine and 720 mm for the -03.

width.sourceNote: OTs-14-4A without a grenade launcher; 75 mm with one fitted.

height.sourceNote: OTs-14-4A without a grenade launcher, as published.

barrelLength.sourceNote: Groza-4, the 9x39mm model. The 7.62x39mm Groza-1 has a 420 mm barrel.

cyclicRate.sourceNote: The article gives a range of 700 to 750 rounds a minute; the midpoint is recorded here because a PropertyValue holds one number.

effectiveRange.sourceNote: Groza-4. The 7.62x39mm Groza-1 is given as 300 m.

sightGraduation.sourceNote: The rear aperture sight in the carrying handle is a tangent leaf graduated from 50 to 200 m.

capacity.sourceNote: 20-round detachable box, shared with the OTs-12 rifle.

images.alt: A colour illustration of a compact bullpup weapon seen from the left against a plain ground. The magazine sits behind the pistol grip, an orange-brown vertical foregrip stands well forward under the barrel, a heavy carrying handle with a tubular body runs along the top, and a short butt pad closes the rear of the receiver.
images.caption: An illustration of the OTs-14-4A-01, the configuration with the vertical foregrip fitted in place of the grenade launcher. Everything behind the trigger is receiver: the magazine sits where a conventional rifle's action would be, which is what makes a 240 mm barrel fit in a 565 mm weapon.

images.alt: A man in a black balaclava, black winter jacket and black gloves crouching in snow beside a hedge, shouldering a bullpup weapon with a wooden-coloured handguard visible under the carrying handle and a wide tube under the barrel. The photograph carries a small watermark in the corner.
images.caption: A Groza shouldered, with the grenade-launcher grip unit fitted — the tube below the barrel. The photograph is watermarked by the uploader's source and is the only freely licensed picture found of the weapon in use.
